definition: Vasodilation is the widening of blood vessels. In the source context, persistent vasodilation contributes to low blood pressure because the vessels remain poorly responsive even when the body’s usual blood-pressure-raising systems are activated.

reasons: The packet supports persistent vasodilation as a mechanism in septic shock, but it does not support the general dictionary-style definition that vasodilation is the widening of blood vessels.
The second sentence is source-specific and narrower than the entry’s wording; it presents the phenomenon in septic shock, not a general definition of vasodilation in all contexts.
